qualification: The first long-span production diagnostic passed all four content/pixel captures but did not execute the proposed CPU path; no matched instruction cohort followed and no page credit is claimed. A widened 32-pixel prototype improved mixed pixels but regressed repeated halfway ties by 14.266% at 32 pixels; every raw result and hash-authenticated intermediate source is retained. The final policy bypasses half opacity and caches its process-start environment control with atomic shared native state. Five final runtime selections pass all prior pixel oracles plus four-thread first-use/boundary cases. Both native integration builds use the identical final header; their passing checks are retained without rerun after only the standalone C test gains concurrent cases. The final benchmark records five span widths, two separate execution diagnostics and four fresh-process unprofiled samples per width, with all output bytes matching the independent oracle and checksums agreeing. Mixed-pixel medians improve 10.968–11.997%, mixed-empty-opaque 5.508–6.655%, opaque 1.779–2.723%. The half-opacity fallback varies by at most 0.007% in this component. No unit-opacity negative-control reduction is credited: the per-row preexisting unit-opacity environment lookup scans the extra control flag and introduces a detectable environment-cost difference. Empty controls are essentially neutral. Input generation, oracle, comparisons and checksums lie outside counters. No broad-suite, live-site, rendering-time, scrolling or 5%-below-Brave claim.
